safi-cedvel:1-7.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها المدّثّر) is like يأيّها المزمّل [Note: In verse (1) of the previous sūra.], (الفاء) conjunction ...
The clause «النداء ...» (the vocative) has no grammatical position: an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «قم ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the vocative.
The clause «أنذر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قم.
(الواو) conjunction in the five places, and likewise (الفاء) [Note: This fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) according to al-Fārisī, and according to others it is the answer of an implied (muqaddar) (أمّا), i.e. "and as for your Lord, magnify (Him)"..
Ibn Hishām rejected that in al-Mughnī, because it involves one omission after another.. since (أمّا) is a substitute for (مهما يكن من شيء), so when it is omitted from the speech it is not replaced by anything, and there is no indication of its omission.. So it is then a conjunction that conjoins the verb after it to an implied verb, namely قم, or تنبّه, or the like.], (ربّك) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being كبّر, and (ثيابك, الرجز) are the two objects of (طهّر, اهجر) respectively; (لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive (majzūm); (لربّك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اصبر). The clause «كبّر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied clause that is conjoined to the clause that answers the vocative, قم.. i.e. "arise, and magnify your Lord".
The clause «طهّر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to another implied clause, i.e. قم.
The clause «اهجر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to another implied clause, i.e. قم.
The clause «لا تمنن ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to one of the request clauses.
The clause «تستكثر ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of تمنن.
The clause «اصبر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to another implied clause, i.e. قم.

* Morphology:
(1) المدّثّر: active participle of the five-letter verb تدثّر, i.e. he put on the دثار, which is the garment.. i.e. the one wrapped in his garments. In it the tāʾ of the pattern تفعّل has been changed into a dāl for assimilation; its pattern is متفعّل [Note: See verse (1) of Sūrat al-Muzzammil.].
(5) الرجز: with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and it is the same as الرجز with kasra on it.. see verse (59) of Sūrat al-Baqara.

* Rhetoric:
Metonymy (al-kināya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَثِيابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ».
It was said: it is a metonymy for a command to purify the soul of deeds that are found filthy and states that are found repugnant. One says "So-and-so is clean of hem and sleeves" when they describe him as free of faults and of the stains of character.
The loose metaphor (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَالرُّجْزَ فَاهْجُرْ».
The literal meaning of الرجز is severe punishment, and what is meant here is the worship of idols. So it was expressed by الرجز — which is severe punishment — because it is caused by the worship of idols; thus the relation of this figure is causation (al-musabbabiyya).

safi-cedvel:8-10.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (في الناقور) the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (يومئذ) an adverb, accusative — or indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, because it is annexed to an indeclinable word, in the position of an accusative — badal (substitute) of إذا [Note: Or a badal of the mubtadaʾ (ذلك), so it is in the position of a nominative.], and إذ is an adverbial noun, indeclinable, in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the tanwīn is the tanwīn of compensation; (يوم) khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (ذلك), nominative; (على الكافرين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (عسير) [Note: Or attached to an adjective of it, or attached to a ḥāl of the pronoun in عسير.]; (غير) a second naʿt (adjective).
The clause «نقر في الناقور ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ذلك ... يوم عسير» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.

* Morphology:
(الناقور): a noun meaning الصور — which is the horn; its pattern is فاعول, from النقر, which is striking.
(عسير): a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral عسر, of the pattern-class فرح and the pattern-class كرم; its pattern is فعيل.

safi-cedvel:11-15.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (من) relative noun, in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the position of the yāʾ in (ذرني); (وحيدا) ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted returning pronoun, i.e. "the one whom I created alone"; (له) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governor being جعلت, and the second (له) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مهّدت); (تمهيدا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative; (أن) a particle that forms a maṣdar and makes the verb accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أزيد ...) is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (يطمع), i.e. "in that I increase him" or "for that I increase him".
The clause «ذرني ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «خلقت ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «جعلت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause خلقت.
The clause «مهّدت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause خلقت.
The clause «يطمع ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause مهّدت.
The clause «أزيد ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(11) وحيدا: a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral وحد, of the pattern-class ضرب..
It also comes, irregularly, from the pattern-class وحد يحد, with ḍamma on the middle radical in the past and kasra in the imperfect; its pattern is فعيل.
(14) تمهيدا: the regular maṣdar of the four-letter verb (مهّد); its pattern is تفعيل, with fatḥa on the tāʾ.

* Benefits:
- Disbelief and obstinacy:
When Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ (حم تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم) up to His saying (المصير), the Prophet ﷺ stood in the mosque praying, while al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra was near him, listening to his recitation. When the Prophet ﷺ perceived that he was listening, he repeated the recitation of the verse. Al-Walīd went off until he came to the assembly of his people of Banū Makhzūm, and said: "By Allah, I have just heard from Muhammad speech that is not of the speech of humans, nor of the speech of the jinn. By Allah, it has a sweetness, and upon it is a grace; its top is fruitful and its bottom is abundant; it rises high and nothing rises above it." Then he went off to his home, and Quraysh said: "By Allah, al-Walīd has turned apostate, and all of Quraysh will surely turn apostate." Abū Jahl said: "I will take care of him for you." So he went off until he sat at al-Walīd's side, looking sad. Al-Walīd said to him: "Why do I see you sad, O son of my brother?" He said: "And what keeps me from being sad, when here are Quraysh collecting money for you to help you in your old age, and they claim that you have embellished Muhammad's speech, and that you go in to Ibn Abī Kabsha and Ibn Abī Quḥāfa to get some of their leftover food." Al-Walīd became angry and said: "Does Quraysh not know that I am among the richest of them in wealth and children? And have Muhammad and his companions ever had their fill of food, that they should have leftover food?" Then he got up with Abū Jahl until he came to the assembly of his people, and said to them: "You claim that Muhammad is mad; have you ever seen him rage?" They said: "By Allah, no." He said: "You claim that he is a soothsayer; have you ever seen him practise soothsaying?" They said: "By Allah, no." He said: "You claim that he is a poet; have you ever seen him utter poetry?" They said: "By Allah, no." He said: "You claim that he is a liar; have you ever found anything of lying in him?" They said: "By Allah, no." Then Quraysh said to al-Walīd: "So what is he?" He thought to himself, then said:
"He is nothing but a sorcerer. Have you not seen him separate a man from his family, his children and his clients? So he is a sorcerer, and what he says is sorcery handed down." That is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: «إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ. فَقُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ. ثُمَّ قُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ. ثُمَّ نَظَرَ. ثُمَّ عَبَسَ وَبَسَرَ. ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ وَاسْتَكْبَرَ. فَقالَ إِنْ هذا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ». When he said that, the assembly shook with joy, and they dispersed marvelling at him.

safi-cedvel:16-25.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) a particle of deterrence and rebuke; (لآياتنا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (عنيدا), meaning (جاحدا) "denying"; (صعودا) tamyīz (specification), accusative.
The clause «إنّه كان لآياتنا ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for the deterrence.
The clause «كان لآياتنا ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar (predicate) of the (first) إنّ.
The clause «سأرهقه ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
(الواو) conjunction, and likewise (الفاء) and (ثمّ) in the four places; (كيف) interrogative noun, in the position of an accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), its governor being قدّر.
The clause «إنّه فكّر ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «فكّر ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar of the (second) إنّ.
The clause «قدّر ...» is in the position of a nominative: conjoined to the clause فكّر.
The clause «قتل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّه فكّر.
The clause «قدّر ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption.
The clause «قتل (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قتل (the first).
The clause «قدّر (the second)» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption emphasizing the first.
The clause «نظر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the second clause قدّر [Note: Or conjoined to the first clause قدّر, so it is in the position of a nominative, and what lies between the two clauses is parenthetical.].
The clause «عبس ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نظر.
The clause «بسر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause عبس — or نظر —.
The clause «أدبر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause عبس.
The clause «استكبر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause عبس.
(الفاء) conjunction; (إن) a particle of negation; (إلّا) for restriction (al-ḥaṣr); and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to سحر; (إن هذا إلّا قول) is like إن هذا إلّا سحر..
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause استكبر.
The clause «إن هذا إلّا سحر ...» is in the position of an accusative: the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إن هذا إلّا قول ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «يؤثر ...» is in the position of a nominative: naʿt (adjective) of سحر.

* Morphology:
(صعودا): with fatḥa on the ṣād, a noun meaning the arduous mountain-path, or the hardship of punishment; its pattern is فعول, with fatḥa then ḍamma.

safi-cedvel:26-30.t:
* I'rab:
(سقر) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative [Note: Or it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. «في سقر», by making (أصليه) carry the meaning of أحرقه "I will burn him".], and it is denied tanwīn because of being a proper name and feminine.
The clause «سأصليه سقر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be a badal (substitute) of (سأرهقه صعودا).].
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) interrogative noun, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) in both places; (سقر) khabar (predicate) of the second.
The clause «ما أدراك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: It may be parenthetical between the ḥāl and its governor — or the one it describes —, and the parenthesis is for magnifying and making it awesome.].
The clause «أدراك ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما).
The clause «ما سقر ...» is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the object of the verb أدراك, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
(لا) negative; (الواو) conjunction; and the object of (تبقي) and (تذر) is omitted; (لوّاحة) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هي; (البشر) genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi of the intensive form لوّاحة, and (اللام) is for strengthening (al-taqwiya); (عليها) attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (تسعة عشر) two numeral parts, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of a nominative as delayed mubtadaʾ.
The clause «لا تبقي ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or in the position of an accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of the second سقر, the governor of it being the sense of magnification in His saying ما سقر.. or a ḥāl of the first سقر.
(3, 4) Or in the position of an accusative as ḥāl of the second or the first سقر].
The clause «لا تذر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لا تبقي.
The clause «(هي) لوّاحة ...» has no grammatical position: another explanatory resumption «3».
The clause «عليها تسعة عشر ...» has no grammatical position: another explanatory resumption «4».

* Morphology:
(29) (لوّاحة): feminine of لوّاح, an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālagha) from لاح يلوح, meaning "it altered the skin", or meaning "it appeared" [Note: This meaning makes the (اللام) in His saying للبشر a preposition attached to (لوّاحة).]; and اللوح is also severe thirst.. Its pattern is فعّال, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(البشر): plural of بشرة, meaning skin. A non-derived noun (ism jāmid); its pattern is فعلة, with fatḥa on the fāʾ, the ʿayn and the lām, and the pattern of البشر is فعل, with two fatḥas.. And البشر may be a collective noun for people.

* Rhetoric:
The art of ambiguity (fann al-ibhām): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «عَلَيْها تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ». This art is that the speaker says something that bears two different meanings, neither of which is distinguished from the other. In this noble verse there are several possible meanings, among them: that the nature of this number, falling one short of the set of twenty, is such that whoever does not believe in Allah and His wisdom is put to trial by it, and objects and mocks, and does not submit as the believer submits, even if the wisdom behind it is hidden from him. It is as though it were said: We have made their number a number whose nature is to be a trial, for the sake of the believer's certainty and the disbeliever's bewilderment, and the certainty of the People of the Book, because their number is nineteen in the two Scriptures, so when they hear the like of it in the Qur'an they become certain that it is sent down from Allah; and the believers' increase in faith through their affirming that, just as they affirmed everything else that was sent down.

* Benefits:
- Omission of the tamyīz (specification):
The tamyīz is omitted when it is understood from the context of the speech, as in the verse we are dealing with (عَلَيْها تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ), i.e. nineteen angels. And in our saying (كم صمت), i.e. how many days did you fast. And the saying of the Exalted: (إِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صابِرُونَ). It is irregular in the chapter of (نعم), as in «من توضأ يوم الجمعة فبها ونعمت», i.e. he has taken the concession, and an excellent concession it is.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative in the four places; (إلّا) for restriction (al-ḥaṣr) in the four places; (ملائكة) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and likewise (فتنة); (للذين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (فتنة); (اللام) of reason (al-taʿlīl); (يستيقن) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; and (الواو) in (أوتوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) in both places; (يزداد) imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يستيقن).. (إيمانا) tamyīz (specification).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يستيقن ...) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to the second (جعلنا).
(الواو) conjunction; (لا) negative; (يرتاب) imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يستيقن); (ليقول) is like ليستيقن; (في قلوبهم) attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (مرض); (ماذا) interrogative noun, in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being أراد [Note: Or (ما) is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ; (ذا) a relative noun, khabar; and the clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause أراد is the ṣila (relative clause) of ذا.]; (بهذا) attached to (أراد); (مثلا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the demonstrative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يقول..) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to the second (جعل), so it is conjoined to the first maṣdar.
(كذلك) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its governor being يضلّ; (من) relative noun, in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi in both places, of the two verbs of misguiding and guiding; (هو) detached pronoun, in the position of a nominative as fāʿil (agent) of (يعلم); (هي) detached pronoun, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ, its khabar being (ذكرى); (للبشر) attached to (ذكرى).
The clause «ما جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ما جعلنا (the second) ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the first relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يستيقن ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «أوتوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the third relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يزداد ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يستيقن.
The clause «لا يرتاب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يستيقن.
The clause «أوتوا.. (the second)» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the fourth relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يقول ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «في قلوبهم مرض ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the fifth relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أراد ...» is in the position of an accusative: the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يضلّ الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يشاء ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the first relative noun (من).
The clause «يهدي ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يضلّ.
The clause «يشاء (the second) ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative noun (من). The clause «ما يعلم ... إلّا هو» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يضلّ الله..
The clause «ما هي إلّا ذكرى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clauses يضلّ الله..

* Morphology:
(يرتاب): it contains a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its original form is يرتيب: the yāʾ was vowelled and what preceded it had fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif, and the conversion carries over from the past tense ارتاب; its pattern is يفتعل.

* Benefits:
Preference (al-tarjīḥ):
Sometimes two valid analyses occur in i'rab, but we judge one of the two to be preferred on the basis of another usage that testifies to it in a parallel place. An example of that is what Makkī said about the saying of the Exalted: (ماذا أَرادَ اللَّهُ بِهذا مَثَلًا يُضِلُّ بِهِ كَثِيراً): that the clause (يضلّ) is an adjective of (مثلا) or resumptive. The correct one is the second analysis, namely resumption, because of the saying of the Exalted in Sūrat al-Muddaththir, in the verse we are dealing with: (ماذا أَرادَ اللَّهُ بِهذا مَثَلًا؟ كَذلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ).

safi-cedvel:32-37.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) a particle of deterrence and rebuke [Note: Al-Jalāl al-Maḥallī made it an opening particle meaning ألا, and al-Farrāʾ and some of the Basrans made it carry the meaning of the answering particle that precedes an oath, (إي), with kasra on the hamza.]; (الواو) the wāw of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم; (الواو) conjunction in both places; (الليل, الصبح) conjoined to القمر, genitive; (إذ) an adverb of past time, in the position of an accusative, attached to the omitted verb of oath; (إذا) an adverb of future time, stripped of condition, in the position of an accusative, attached to the implied verb of oath; and the pronoun is the noun of (إنّ), referring to سقر; (اللام) for emphasis, in the place of the lām of oath, in compensation for the shifted lām (al-muzaḥlaqa); (إحدى) khabar (predicate) of إنّ, nominative..
The clause «(أقسم) بالقمر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أدبر ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أسفر ...» is in the position of a genitive, by (إذا) being annexed to it.
The clause «إنّها لإحدى ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of the oath.
(نذيرا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of إحدى, its governor being the emphasis [Note: The word comes in the masculine because إحدى is made to carry the meaning of punishment.. It was said that it is a ḥāl of the pronoun in إحدى, its governor being the sense of magnification, i.e. "the greatest of the great things, as a warning".. It was said that it is a ḥāl of الكبر or of its pronoun..
They allowed it to be a tamyīz (specification), by making it a maṣdar meaning الإنذار "warning", like نكير meaning الإنكار.. or it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, if it is a maṣdar..]; (للبشر) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نذيرا); (لمن) badal (substitute) of البشر, with repetition of the preposition; (منكم) attached to a ḥāl of the returning pronoun; (أن) a particle that forms a maṣdar and makes the verb accusative; (أو) a conjunction.
The clause «شاء ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «يتقدّم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتقدّم) is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb شاء.
The clause «يتأخّر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يتقدّم.

* Morphology:
(35) الكبر: plural of كبري, feminine of أكبر; its pattern is فعل, with ḍamma then fatḥa. [Translator's note: the source prints كبري; the usual spelling is كبرى.]

safi-cedvel:38-42.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted.]; (إلّا) for exception; (أصحاب) excepted by إلّا, accusative [Note: The exception is connected (muttaṣil), from كلّ نفس.. It was said it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), by interpreting the meaning as "every disbelieving soul is held for its deeds in the Fire".]..
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كسبت) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (رهينة), meaning مرهونة "pledged".
(في جنّات) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of يتساءلون [Note: Or attached to an omitted khabar, its implied form being هم, and the clause is an explanatory resumption.]; (عن المجرمين) attached to (يتساءلون), with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "about the state of the criminals"; (ما) interrogative noun, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being the clause سلككم; (في سقر) attached to (سلككم), i.e. "made you enter".
The clause «كلّ نفس.. رهينة» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كسبت ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «يتساءلون» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «ما سلككم ...» is in the position of an accusative: the object of speech of an implied verb of saying, i.e.:
"They say after that: ما سلككم".. and the implied clause of saying is resumptive.
The clause «سلككم ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما).

* Morphology:
(38) رهينة: feminine of رهين — see verse (21) of Sūrat al-Ṭūr — a derived adjective. It is better left without being interpreted in the sense of a passive participle — since فعيل in the sense of مفعول does not take the feminine tāʾ, but masculine and feminine are the same in it — and it may be a maṣdar used to mean the object, like الشتيمة — on the view of al-Zamakhsharī — who said: because Allah the Exalted made the obligation laid on His servants like a debt upon them, and their souls are pledged.

safi-cedvel:43-47.t:
* I'rab:
(نك) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the sukūn appearing on the nūn that is omitted for lightening; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being نحن [Translator's note: the source prints تقديمه, evidently for تقديره "its implied form".]; (من المصلّين) attached to the khabar (predicate) of نك; (الواو) conjunction in the three places; (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نخوض).
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لم نك ...» is in the position of an accusative: the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لم نك (the second)» is in the position of an accusative: conjoined to the clause لم نك (the first).
The clause «نطعم ...» is in the position of an accusative: khabar of نك.
The clause «كنّا نخوض ...» is in the position of an accusative: conjoined to the clause لم نك (the first).
The clause «نخوض ...» is in the position of an accusative: khabar of كنّا.
(بيوم) attached to (نكذّب); (حتّى) a particle of limit and a preposition..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أتانا ...) is in the position of a genitive by (حتّى), attached to the four actions: not praying, not feeding, plunging in vain talk, and denying..
The clause «كنّا نكذّب ...» is in the position of an accusative: conjoined to the clause that is the object of speech.
The clause «نكذّب ...» is in the position of an accusative: khabar of (the second) كنّا.
The clause «أتانا اليقين» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(الخائضين): plural of الخائض, active participle of the triliteral خاض; its pattern is فاعل. In it the weak middle radical is regularly changed into a hamza; its original form is خاوض: the wāw came after the quiescent alif of فاعل, so it was turned into a hamza..

safi-cedvel:48-48.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the answer of an implied condition; (ما) negative.
The clause «ما تنفعهم شفاعة ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of an implied condition, i.e. "if this is their state, then no intercession will benefit them"..

* Rhetoric:
The art of negating a thing by affirming it (nafy al-shayʾ bi-ījābih): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «فَما تَنْفَعُهُمْ شَفاعَةُ الشَّافِعِينَ».
This art is that the speaker affirms something in the outward sense of his speech, on condition that what is affirmed is borrowed, then negates something connected with it figuratively, while what is negated in reality lies in the inner sense of the speech.
So in this noble verse the meaning is not that someone intercedes for them but the intercession of those who intercede for them does not benefit them; rather the meaning is the negation of intercession, and so the benefit is negated, i.e. they have no intercession that might benefit them.

safi-cedvel:49-51.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) interrogative noun, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (لهم) attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); (عن التذكرة) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (معرضين), which is a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the pronoun in (لهم); (من قسورة) attached to (فرّت).
The clause «ما لهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كأنّهم حمر ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl of the pronoun in معرضين, so it is an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila).
The clause «فرّت ...» is in the position of a nominative: second naʿt (adjective) of حمر [Note: Or in the position of an accusative as ḥāl of حمر, because it is particularized by the adjective, with قد implied, with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the time of Allah's will", attached to (يذكرون).] [Translator's note: the second half of this footnote ("with the omission of a muḍāf … attached to (يذكرون)") appears to belong to verse 56 (إلّا أن يشاء الله); it is translated as printed.].

* Morphology:
(50) مستنفرة: feminine of مستنفر, active participle of the six-letter verb استنفر; its pattern is مستفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(51) قسورة: a non-derived noun (ism jāmid) meaning the lion, or a collective noun meaning the band of archers, having no singular from its own root.. And among the Arabs everything large and strong is a قسورة; its pattern is فعللة, with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
The unqualified simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «كَأَنَّهُمْ حُمُرٌ مُسْتَنْفِرَةٌ».
He likened them, in their turning away from the Qur'an and from listening to the reminder and the admonition, to donkeys that have fled from their enclosure because of what frightened them. In likening them to donkeys there is evident blame and a clear disparagement of their state, as in the saying of the Exalted: «كَمَثَلِ الْحِمارِ يَحْمِلُ أَسْفاراً», and a testimony against them of dull-wittedness and little intelligence; and you see nothing like the bolting of wild asses and their running on and on when something alarms them.

safi-cedvel:52-53.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); (منهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (كلّ امرئ); (أن) a particle that forms a maṣdar and makes the verb accusative, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun.
The clause «يريد كلّ امرئ ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يؤتى ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يؤتى ...) is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb يريد.
(كلّا) a particle of deterrence and rebuke; (لا) negative.
The clause «لا يخافون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(يؤتى): it contains a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its original form is يؤتي — with a vowelled yāʾ at its end preceded by a tāʾ with fatḥa —: the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif.
(منشّرة): feminine of منشّر, passive participle of the four-letter verb نشّر; its pattern is مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:54-56.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction; (من) a conditional noun making the verb jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (أن) a particle that forms a maṣdar and makes the verb accusative..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يشاء الله) is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يذكرون), i.e. "except by the will of Allah" [Note: Or it is in the position of an accusative as an adverb of time.].
The clause «إنّه تذكرة ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «من شاء ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «شاء ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «ذكره ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يذكرون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يشاء الله ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «هو أهل ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(56) التقوى: it stands in for the interpreted maṣdar in the passive, i.e. "worthy that He be feared"..
